title: The World Wars and the Cold War: 1914-1991

questions.question: The spark for World War I was the assassination at Sarajevo (28 June 1914) of:
options: Archduke Franz Ferdinand by Gavrilo Princip
questions.rationale: Gavrilo Princip of the Black Hand killed Archduke Franz Ferdinand, heir to Austria-Hungary, at Sarajevo on 28 June 1914 — the spark that the alliance cascade turned into general war.

questions.question: The MAIN acronym for World War I's causes stands for:
questions.rationale: Militarism, Alliances, Imperialism, and Nationalism are the standard deep causes — with the Anglo-German naval race and Balkan nationalism as prime examples.

questions.question: The United States entered World War I in April 1917 largely because of:
options: The Zimmermann telegram and unrestricted U-boat warfare
questions.rationale: Unrestricted submarine warfare (including the Lusitania sinking of 1915) and the Zimmermann telegram's proposed German-Mexican alliance brought America into the war in April 1917.

questions.question: The Treaty of Versailles' Article 231:
options: Assigned war guilt to Germany and its allies
questions.rationale: The war guilt clause made Germany responsible, justifying reparations of 132 billion gold marks and territorial losses — the resentment Hitler later exploited.

questions.question: The Great Depression began with:
options: The Wall Street Crash of October 1929
questions.rationale: The October 1929 crash collapsed banks and world trade, with a quarter of US workers jobless — the economic despair that incubated fascism and Nazism.

questions.question: Mussolini's Fascists took power in Italy through:
questions.rationale: After the March on Rome (October 1922), King Victor Emmanuel III invited Mussolini to form a government — constitutional in form, dictatorial in substance.

questions.question: Which battle of February 1943 destroyed the German Sixth Army and turned the tide in Europe?
questions.rationale: Stalingrad's surrender in February 1943 destroyed the Sixth Army after the failure of Barbarossa's 1941 gamble — the war's European turning point.

questions.question: The United Nations was founded on 24 October 1945 with how many permanent members of the Security Council?
questions.rationale: Five permanent, veto-wielding members: the USA, USSR (now Russia), Britain, France, and China — the lesson of the League's unanimity rule applied differently.

questions.question: The Truman Doctrine and the Marshall Plan, both of 1947, were instruments of:
questions.rationale: Containment — armed by Truman Doctrine aid to Greece and Turkey and Marshall Plan reconstruction — defined US Cold War policy from 1947.

questions.question: The Non-Aligned Movement's 1961 founding summit at Belgrade was led by:
questions.rationale: Nehru of India, Nasser of Egypt, and Tito of Yugoslavia led the Belgrade founding (1961), offering the decolonising world a path outside both blocs.
